channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Freight Brokers Need a Safety Net After Supreme Court Ruling
item.description: US freight brokers are still a bit dazed and confused from a bombshell Supreme Court ruling in May that clarified whether these cargo matchmakers should be held liable for truck accidents.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Texas Power Grid Is Being Transformed by Solar Power
item.description: It seems the Trumpian recession in US green energy fails to apply to one of the more Trumpian areas of the country: Texas. Solar power and batteries are taking large bites out of America’s biggest state power grid in the US, and helping to suppress electricity prices in the process.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: The US Military Is Running Out of Weapons. Thank Congress
item.description: “Protecting our nation from those who would do us harm is the first and most important responsibility of government.” That’s from the website of Senator Amy Klobuchar, a Minnesota Democrat. But it could be any lawmaker, or any president, Democrat or Republican. Almost all proclaim it, and by their own standard, almost all are failing — as they have for years, with no end in sight.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: TWG Global Episode Proves Americans' Annuities Deserve Oversight
item.description: Every year, Americans send hundreds of billions of dollars of retirement savings to life insurers in return for annuities that promise a future income. It’s an industry built on trust and prudence.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: MAHA’s Strange Pivot to Its Least-Popular Ideas
item.description: “Bobby Unleashed” is the West Wing’s midterms motto, according to reporting by Politico. But what exactly is Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. being unleashed to do? Because the biggest MAHA policy reforms have run into that familiar Washington foe: old-fashioned bureaucracy. And while many Americans still do want to “Make America Healthy Again,” there are now plenty of other concerns competing for voters’ attention.
item.dc:creator: Abby McCloskey

item.title: UN Report on 1.5C Overshoot: Global Warming Is Still in Our Hands
item.description: A popular metaphor for climate change is the boiling frog, the idea being that we’re getting cooked so slowly that we don’t realize it until it’s too late. In reality, if humans are the frogs, they’re not just being cooked alive and already feeling it, they’re reaching out of the pot to crank up the burner.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: Fed Credibility Depends on Resisting Politics, Not Playing It
item.description: At Jackson Hole last month, all eyes were on Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh in his first speech at the Fed’s annual conference. But all thoughts were about the Fed’s rate decision next week.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Sahm

item.title: Trump’s Iran War Forgot About Nukes
item.description: When was the last time you heard a meaningful proposal to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear arsenal?
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Leipzig Drone Attack Shows Putin Has the West in His Grip
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has won another tactical and psychological victory in his quasi-war against NATO and the West. The skirmish took place at the airport of Leipzig, a large logistics hub that supplies NATO’s eastern flank and Ukraine, where German authorities last month defused an armed drone that was about to attack a Ukrainian aircraft parked nearby.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Britain Has an Easy Way to Win on Cheap Electricity
item.description: In his six weeks at No. 10 Downing Street, Andy Burnham has skilfully avoided making unpopular or divisive decisions. His predecessor as UK prime minister began his tenure by saying things were awful and kept reminding us that they might well get worse. Burnham has been as sunny as this year’s summer.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Bond Yields: It’s Still Endless Summer
item.description: But a discontinuous shock could upset this return to normality.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Melenchon and the AfD Are Setting the Stage for an Epic Fight Over the Euro
item.description: This week the European Central Bank will meet to decide a probable interest-rate hike at a critical time for the euro economy. Rising headline inflation, not helped by the war in the Strait of Hormuz, will be uppermost on the rate setters’ minds. But their job is getting harder because of the surging support for populist parties in Germany and France.
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: Warsh Doctrine Is Ill-Suited for a Fading Thailand
item.description: You could call the head of Thailand’s central bank the anti-Kevin Warsh. As officials in major economies shy away from anything other than the basics of controlling inflation and boosting employment, Vitai Ratanakorn is willing to tackle broader problems. To succeed, he'll need good fortune — and the indulgence of politicians who gave him the job.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: You Don't Have to Trust Chinese AI
item.description: When DeepSeek’s reasoning model burst onto the scene last year and put Chinese artificial intelligence on the global map, the internet responded by probing its views on Taiwan or Tiananmen Square.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: China’s Bond Rally Has One Collateral Damage
item.description: A global selloff in government bonds is igniting concerns over higher mortgage repayments and corporate financing costs. While China is an outlier to this trend, lower-rates-for-longer may not necessarily be good news, either.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: Alaska Senate Race: Doubts About Democrats Are Republicans’ Best Asset
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has many things breaking her way in her bid to unseat Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska. But Sullivan has one big thing working for him. Whether that’s enough will likely determine whether he wins reelection — while also offering clues about the fate of other red-state Republican senators this year.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein
